purpose: Keep observed environmental signals, company actions, industry technical references, and company future direction as independent evidence layers, then propose review questions only where layers overlap. Timing overlap never becomes a causal claim.

layers.OBSERVED: Source-native public environmental data and mathematically detected multi-year signals.
layers.COMPANY_ACTION: Company/site actions, investments, permits, certifications or completed/ongoing management activities supported by company or official evidence.
layers.INDUSTRY_TECHNICAL: BAT/K-BREF or other industry technical references. Document availability alone is not semantic evidence of a particular technique.
layers.FUTURE_DIRECTION: Company-stated targets, strategies, planned projects or future milestones. A plan is not an achieved outcome.

candidate_policy.MULTI_LAYER_REVIEW: An observed signal plus at least two independently supported non-observed layers overlap by environmental domain and compatible scope.
candidate_policy.FOUR_LAYER_READY: Observed signal, company action, semantically extracted industry technical evidence, and future direction are all present. This still permits only a review hypothesis, not causality.
candidate_policy.CONTEXT_ONLY: Observed signal has one additional layer or the industry reference is only document-level metadata.
candidate_policy.OBSERVED_ONLY: Only a numeric/public-data signal is present.

scope_rules: SITE evidence may link only to the same canonical site or to company-wide evidence.
COMPANY evidence may provide context to any requested-scope site, but must remain labeled company-wide.
Raw company-wide evidence is preserved; human review candidates follow Requested_Scope.json.
time_rules: Overlapping or adjacent years are context only.
A later company target may explain what management intends to address, not why an earlier signal occurred.
Publication year and activity/effective year must remain distinct when available.
hard_boundaries: Do not state that a company action caused an observed environmental change from temporal overlap alone.
Do not state that a company applies a BAT from the existence of an industry BAT document.
Do not treat a future strategy or MOU as completed environmental performance.
Do not rank environmental importance by a single quantity or a hidden composite score.
When a required layer is missing, output a concrete study/verification question instead of filling the gap with inference.
